fixtures.reason: Baseline v0.5 signed envelope (no facets, no claims) verifies under Signature Profile A.

Baseline v0.5 signed envelope (no facets, no claims) verifies under Signature Profile B (JCS + ES256; EXT-OPT Section O15). The signing input is byte-identical to Profile A (Section 1.6.3) - only the signature primitive differs. signature.value is the base64url of the 64-byte raw R || S (EXT-OPT Section O15.1).

ACCEPT: a genuine Profile B signature whose S component is deliberately above n/2 ("high-S"). Profile B imposes NO low-S rule and NO RFC 6979 requirement (EXT-OPT Section O15.2): Secure Enclave / StrongBox / TPM signers expose no nonce control and do not guarantee low-S, so a canonical-S rule would make every hardware-resident key non-conformant. An evaluator that rejects this fixture has added a malleability check the profile forbids and fails the suite.

Reject: cryptographically wrong signature.value (bit-flipped after signing). Ed25519 verification over the Section 1.6.3 signing input MUST fail; freshness is not reached (not-evaluated, Section 3.3.1). A signature-presence-only implementation accepts this fixture and fails the suite.
Reject: subject mutated after signing. The signature no longer covers the canonical bytes (Section 1.6.3/1.6.4); verification MUST fail.
Reject: embedded publicKeySpkiB64 substituted with a foreign key after signing (the Section 1.6.4 key-substitution attack). Verification against the embedded key MUST fail.
Reject: now > expiresAt (Section 3.1.2 freshness enforcement). The signature is genuine; only TTL math rejects this fixture.
Reject: issuedAt > expiresAt (Section 3.1.2). Cross-field temporal misuse over a genuine signature.
Reject: issuedAt more than 60 seconds in the future relative to the evaluation clock is rejected with freshnessCheck "stale" (Section 3.1.2).

Reject: manifestVersion "0.5" is not supported by any v0.5 processing path (Section 1.3.1: evaluators MUST check version support before processing). v0.3 envelopes instead take the EXT-T1 Section T1.6.4 backcompat path (see the v03-backcompat fixtures).

Reject: signature.algorithm "ES384" is not a recognized suite; evaluators MUST reject and record signatureCheck "unsupported-profile" (Section 1.5.1/1.6.5). ES384 is a well-formed IANA/JOSE algorithm token that Universal Manifest does not register, so this exercises the unknown-profile path and nothing else: the manifest carries a genuine Ed25519 Profile A signature over a matching Ed25519 SPKI, and only the suite token is unrecognized. Rejection MUST occur at the (algorithm, canonicalization) pair check, before any key or value inspection, and the pair MUST NOT be reinterpreted as a recognized suite. This test is re-keyed off "ES256", which became a recognized suite (Profile B) in v0.5; it stays unconditional because the schema enum structurally rejects any token outside the registered set.

Reject: cryptographically wrong Profile B signature.value (bit-flipped after signing). ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 verification over the Section 1.6.3 signing input MUST fail; freshness is not reached (not-evaluated, Section 3.3.1). A signature-presence-only implementation accepts this fixture and fails the suite.
Reject: subject mutated after Profile B signing. The signature no longer covers the canonical bytes (Section 1.6.3/1.6.4); verification MUST fail.

Reject: embedded publicKeySpkiB64 substituted with a foreign P-256 key after signing (the Section 1.6.4 key-substitution attack). The suite and the key type are both correct - only the key is wrong - so verification against the embedded key MUST fail.

Reject (encoding discipline): the signature is cryptographically genuine but signature.value carries the 72-byte DER/X9.62 encoding instead of the 64-byte raw R || S the profile mandates (EXT-OPT Section O15.1). DER MUST be rejected. Note the required reason code: the (algorithm, canonicalization) pair IS recognized, so this is signatureCheck "invalid" (a malformed value under a recognized profile), NOT "unsupported-profile".

Reject: an Ed25519 SPKI declared under algorithm "ES256". The REQUIRED SPKI-algorithm-vs-algorithm consistency check (EXT-OPT Section O15.4) MUST fail, in either direction. The profile pair is recognized and the value is well-formed, so the reason code is signatureCheck "invalid", NOT "unsupported-profile".
